subject: maths
title: Chapter 5 · Test 4
summary: A 25-minute test on Chapter 5 · Decimals: place value, rounding, the four operations with decimals, and terminating and recurring decimals.
body:
This test covers all of Chapter 5 · Decimals: place value in decimals, rounding decimals, adding and subtracting decimals, multiplying and dividing decimals, and terminating and recurring decimals.

## How to do this test

- Allow about 25 minutes.
- No notes and no calculator unless the question says.
- There are 15 questions: 4 easy, 5 medium, 4 hard and 2 challenge.
- Line up decimal points, count decimal places, and estimate to check your answers make sense.
- When you finish, read the worked steps for any question you got wrong, then go back to that lesson.

questions.prompt: In the number 8.536, which digit is in the hundredths place?
questions.explanation: After the point the places are tenths (5), hundredths (3) and thousandths (6), so the hundredths digit is 3. 5 is the tenths digit — the places after the point start at tenths, not hundredths.
steps: The places after the point are, in order: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
In 8.536 those digits are 5, 3 and 6, so the hundredths digit is 3.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 5 is the first digit after the point, which is the tenths place. Hundredths is the second.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 6 is in the thousandths place. Hundredths is the second place after the point.
mistakes.D: Step 1: 8 is in the ones place, on the left of the point. The places after the point are tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

questions.explanation: The hundredths digit is 7 and the next digit is 5, so the 7 rounds up to 8: 0.08. 0.07 forgets that 5 rounds up.
steps: 2 decimal places: the rounding digit is the hundredths digit, 7.
The deciding digit is the next one: 5.
5 is 5 or more, so round up: 0.08.

mistakes.B: Step 3: the deciding digit is 5, and 5 or more means round up. You just cut off the digits.
mistakes.C: Step 1: you rounded to 1 decimal place. 2 decimal places means keep the hundredths digit.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you kept 3 decimal places. Stop at the hundredths digit.

questions.explanation: Borrowing makes 8.4 into 7 ones and 14 tenths: 14 − 7 = 7 tenths and 7 − 2 = 5 ones, so 5.7. 6.3 subtracts 4 from 7 instead of borrowing. Check: 5.7 + 2.7 = 8.4 ✓
steps: Line up the points. Tenths: 4 − 7 can't be done, so borrow 1 one — 8 ones become 7 ones and 4 tenths become 14 tenths.
Tenths: 14 − 7 = 7.
Ones: 7 − 2 = 5. The answer is 5.7.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you did 7 − 4 because 4 − 7 looked impossible. Borrow 1 from the ones to make 14 tenths.
mistakes.B: Step 3: after borrowing, the 8 ones become 7 ones. You left it as 8.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the sign is − so subtract; you added the numbers.

questions.explanation: 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones and 3 tenths ÷ 3 = 1 tenth, so 2.1. 21 forgets the decimal point. Check: 2.1 × 3 = 6.3 ✓
steps: Set up short division with the point in the answer above the point in 6.3.
Tenths: 3 ÷ 3 = 1, so the answer is 2.1.

mistakes.A: Step 3: keep the point in the answer directly above the point in 6.3. You lost it.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 6 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones, so the 2 goes before the point.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the sign is ÷ but you multiplied by 3.

questions.prompt: Which fraction in simplest form is equal to 0.85?
questions.explanation: 0.85 = 85/100, and dividing top and bottom by 5 gives 17/20. 17/200 starts from thousandths, but 0.85 has only two decimal places. Check: 17 ÷ 20 = 0.85 ✓
steps: 0.85 has two decimal places, so it is 85/100.
The highest common factor of 85 and 100 is 5, so divide both by 5: 17/20.

mistakes.B: Step 1: 0.85 has two decimal places, so start from hundredths (85/100), not thousandths.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 85/10 would be 8.5. 0.85 has two decimal places, so the bottom number is 100.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the digits are not the top and bottom of the fraction. 0.85 means 85 hundredths.

questions.prompt: Estimate 48.7 ÷ 7.2 by first rounding each number to the nearest whole number.
questions.explanation: 48.7 ≈ 49 and 7.2 ≈ 7, so the estimate is 49 ÷ 7 = 7. 6 comes from rounding the wrong way (48 ÷ 8).
steps: Round each number: 48.7 ≈ 49 (tenths digit 7 rounds up) and 7.2 ≈ 7 (tenths digit 2 rounds down).
Divide the rounded numbers: 49 ÷ 7 = 7.

mistakes.A: Step 1: 48.7 rounds to 49 (not 48) and 7.2 rounds to 7 (not 8). Check each deciding digit.
mistakes.B: Step 2: the sign is ÷, so divide the rounded numbers. You subtracted.
mistakes.C: Step 2: the sign is ÷, so divide the rounded numbers. You added.

questions.explanation: With the points lined up: 2.08 + 5.70 + 11.40 = 19.18. 18.18 forgets to carry 1 from the 11 tenths. Check: estimate 2 + 6 + 11 = 19 ✓
steps: Write each with 2 decimal places and line up the points: 2.08, 5.70, 11.40.
Hundredths: 8 + 0 + 0 = 8.
Tenths: 0 + 7 + 4 = 11 — write 1 and carry 1 to the ones.
Ones: 2 + 5 + 1 + 1 (carried) = 9; tens: 1. The answer is 19.18.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you lined up the right-hand ends, so 5.7 and 11.4 were added as 0.57 and 1.14. Line up the points.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 0 + 7 + 4 = 11 tenths, so carry 1 into the ones column. You forgot the carry.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you added 08 + 7 + 4 as whole numbers. Write every number with 2 decimal places first.

questions.explanation: 7 × 6 = 42, and there are 3 decimal places in total, so 0.042. 0.42 only uses 2 decimal places.
steps: Ignore the points and multiply: 7 × 6 = 42.
Count decimal places: 0.07 has 2 and 0.6 has 1 — 3 altogether.
Give 42 three decimal places, adding a zero in front: 0.042.

mistakes.A: Step 2: there are 3 decimal places altogether (2 in 0.07 and 1 in 0.6), not 2.
mistakes.B: Step 2: count again — 0.07 has 2 decimal places and 0.6 has 1, so 3 altogether, not 4.
mistakes.D: Step 3: you multiplied 7 × 6 but never put the decimal point back.

questions.explanation: 4 ÷ 9 = 0.4444… because the remainder 4 keeps coming back, so it is written 0.4̇. 0.4 and 0.44 both stop, but the 4s never end.
steps: The fraction bar means divide: 4 ÷ 9.
40 ÷ 9 = 4 remainder 4 — write 4 in the tenths.
The remainder is 4 again, so 4 repeats forever: 4/9 = 0.444… = 0.4̇.

mistakes.B: Step 1: you divided 9 by 4. The top number is divided by the bottom: 4 ÷ 9.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the remainder never reaches 0, so the decimal keeps going. Show the repeating digit with a dot.
mistakes.D: Step 3: the 4s go on forever, not just twice. Use dot notation to show they repeat.

questions.prompt: How many hundredths are there in 3.4 altogether?
questions.explanation: One whole is 100 hundredths, so 3.4 is 3.4 × 100 = 340 hundredths. 34 counts tenths instead.
steps: There are 100 hundredths in 1 whole, so multiply by 100 to count hundredths.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 34 is the number of tenths in 3.4. Each tenth is 10 hundredths.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 3.4 has 0 in the hundredths place, but the question asks how many hundredths the WHOLE number is worth.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 3400 is the number of thousandths. One whole is 100 hundredths, not 1000.

questions.prompt: Six friends share a bill of $47.15 equally. A calculator shows 7.858333… How much is each share, to the nearest cent?
questions.explanation: Nearest cent means 2 decimal places: in 7.858333… the hundredths digit is 5 and the next digit is 8, so it rounds up to $7.86. $7.85 forgets to round.
steps: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, so round to 2 decimal places.
In 7.858333… the rounding digit is 5 (hundredths) and the deciding digit is 8.
8 is 5 or more, so round up: each share is $7.86.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you cut off the digits after the hundredths. The deciding digit is 8, so the cents round up.
mistakes.B: Step 1: nearest cent means 2 decimal places. You rounded to 1 decimal place first (7.9).
mistakes.C: Step 1: sharing means divide. You multiplied the bill by 6.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses 0.75 kg of flour for each batch. How many batches can be made from 6 kg of flour?
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 0.75: multiply both by 100 to get 600 ÷ 75 = 8. 4.5 multiplies instead of dividing. Check: 8 × 0.75 = 6 ✓
steps: Number of batches = 6 ÷ 0.75.
0.75 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100: 600 ÷ 75.
600 ÷ 75 = 8 batches.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you multiplied 6 by 0.75. To find how many 0.75s fit into 6, divide.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 0.75 × 100 is 75, not 7.5. Multiply both numbers by 100 and check your place values.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you multiplied 6 by 100 but 0.75 by only 10. Multiply both by the same amount.

questions.prompt: Write 7/11 as a decimal using dot notation.
questions.explanation: 7 ÷ 11 = 0.636363…, where the group 63 repeats, so the dots go over the 6 and the 3: 0.6̇3̇. 0.6̇ would mean 0.666…
steps: Divide 7 by 11: 70 ÷ 11 = 6 remainder 4 — write 6.
40 ÷ 11 = 3 remainder 7 — write 3.
The remainder 7 is back to where we started, so 63 repeats: 0.6̇3̇.

mistakes.B: Step 3: one dot over the 6 means only 6 repeats (0.666…). Here the pair 63 repeats.
mistakes.C: Step 3: the remainder never reaches 0, so the decimal keeps going. Show the repeating group with dots.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you divided 11 by 7. The top number is divided by the bottom: 7 ÷ 11.

questions.prompt: 2/13 = 0.153846153846…, where the group 153846 repeats forever. What is the 25th digit after the decimal point?
questions.explanation: The group has 6 digits. 25 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 1, so after 4 full groups (24 digits) the 25th digit is the 1st digit of the group: 1. 6 is the 24th digit.
steps: The repeating group 153846 has 6 digits.
25 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 1, so 4 full groups use 24 digits.
The 25th digit is the 1st digit of the next group, which is 1.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the remainder is 1, so the 25th digit matches the 1st digit of the group, not the 2nd.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 6 is the 24th digit, at the end of the 4th full group. The 25th digit starts a new group.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you used the last digit of 25 to pick the 5th digit. Divide 25 by the group length (6) instead.

questions.prompt: Without working out the exact answers, which of these calculations gives the largest answer?
questions.explanation: 6 × 0.9 and 6 ÷ 1.1 are both less than 6. 6 × 1.1 = 6.6, but 6 ÷ 0.9 = 6.66…, which is a bit more, because dividing by 0.9 adds a ninth of 6 rather than a tenth.
steps: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller: 6 × 0.9 is less than 6.
Dividing by a number more than 1 makes it smaller: 6 ÷ 1.1 is less than 6.
Compare the other two: 6 × 1.1 = 6.6, and 6 ÷ 0.9 = 60 ÷ 9 = 6.66…, so 6 ÷ 0.9 is the largest.

mistakes.A: Step 1: multiplying by a number less than 1 makes 6 smaller, so this is less than 6.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 6 × 1.1 = 6.6 is bigger than 6, but another option is bigger still. Work out each of the two options that are bigger than 6 and compare them.
mistakes.C: Step 2: dividing by a number bigger than 1 makes 6 smaller, so this is less than 6.
